findings.claim: "the Catholic Church has officially recognised 70 cures as miraculous since 1858" (repeated in the key fact, the conclusion, two mark schemes, two flashcards and the glossary)
findings.truth: The recognised total is 72. The most recent recognition was the cure of Antonietta Raco on 16 April 2025.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Sanctuary of Our Lady of Lourdes: "The Roman Catholic Church has officially recognized 72 miraculous healings, the latest of which was the cure of Antonietta Raco, recognised on 16 April 2025."

findings.claim: Key fact: "The Lourdes Medical Bureau has recognised 70 miracles since then."
findings.truth: The Medical Bureau can only declare a cure medically inexplicable. Only the Church can declare a cure a miracle. The lesson's own main paragraph states this correctly, so the key fact contradicts it.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Lourdes Medical Bureau: "CMIL is not entitled to pronounce a cure 'miraculous'; this can only be done by the Church."

findings.claim: "For the 12-mark “Discuss” question ... examiners consistently note that students write only one sentence on the opposing view."
findings.truth: The 12-mark command word is Evaluate, not Discuss. The examiner claim cannot be sourced and is a fabricated examiner-report statement.
findings.evidence: spec command-word table (lines 4280-4340): Evaluate = 12 marks, AO2. No command word Discuss exists in the table.

findings.claim: Question [1] is typed "3 marks — Describe".
findings.truth: The spec sets Describe at 4 marks. Paper 3 questions run (a) outline three, 3 marks; (b) explain two, 4 marks; (c) explain two with a source, 5 marks; (d) evaluate, 12 marks. A 3-mark Describe is not a Paper 3 form.
findings.evidence: spec command-word table (line 4286, Describe = 4 marks); Paper 3 overview (lines 392-432) and assessment notes (line 3324).

findings.claim: Question [4]: "Discuss this statement.", typed "12 marks — Discuss a Statement".
findings.truth: The 12-mark question uses the command word Evaluate.

findings.claim: The glossary tooltip on "Catechism of the Catholic Church" reads "The official teaching authority of the Catholic Church, exercised by the Pope and bishops in union with him."
findings.truth: That is the definition of the Magisterium. The Catechism is the Church's official written summary of its doctrine and moral teaching, cited by paragraph number.
findings.evidence: Catechism of the Catholic Church, prologue and CCC 85-87 (Magisterium); vatican.va Catechism text.

findings.claim: CCC 66-67 quoted as: private revelations can “help us live more fully by it” in a particular era.
findings.truth: CCC 67 reads: "It is not their role to improve or complete Christ's definitive Revelation, but to help live more fully by it in a certain period of history." The lesson adds "us" and paraphrases the closing phrase inside the quotation marks.

findings.claim: "Cardinal Newman famously argued that the orderliness of the cosmos — the fact that evolution follows predictable laws — is itself evidence of a rational mind behind nature."
findings.truth: Newman is known for the opposite position on design: he argued from conscience to God and said he believed in design because he already believed in God, not in God because he saw design. No source supports the argument given here. The edit removes the attribution and does not substitute a new one.
findings.evidence: Attribution could not be corroborated on the permitted sources (Wikipedia, John Henry Newman, has no design-argument material). De-attributed rather than replaced.

findings.claim: "For the 12-mark Discuss, develop the Dawkins/evolution challenge in full".
findings.truth: The 12-mark command word is Evaluate.

findings.claim: Question [1] typed "3 marks — Describe"; question [4] uses "Discuss this statement."
findings.truth: Describe carries 4 marks in the spec and is not a Paper 3 form; the 12-mark command word is Evaluate.

findings.claim: "For the 12-mark Discuss, develop the Humanist counter-argument in full".
findings.truth: The 12-mark command word is Evaluate.

findings.claim: Question [1] typed "3 marks — Describe"; question [4] uses "Discuss this statement."
findings.truth: Describe carries 4 marks in the spec and is not a Paper 3 form; the 12-mark command word is Evaluate.

findings.claim: "This logical tension, sometimes called the Epicurean trilemma".
findings.truth: The usual names are the Epicurean paradox and, in Mackie's form, the inconsistent triad. Trilemma is a loose label but is not wrong enough to cost marks.

findings.claim: "The Catechism 2226 also notes that parents are “the first educators” of their children in the faith" (repeated in the 5-mark scheme, a match knowledge check and a flashcard).
findings.truth: CCC 2226 does not contain the phrase "first educators". It reads: "Education in the faith by the parents should begin in the child's earliest years ... The parish is the Eucharistic community and the heart of the liturgical life of Christian families; it is a privileged place for the catechesis of children and parents."

findings.claim: "many Protestant denominations and the Church of England now affirm same-sex partnerships".
findings.truth: The Church of England does not marry same-sex couples; its canons still define marriage as between one man and one woman. In February 2023 the General Synod approved Prayers of Love and Faith, which allow clergy to bless same-sex couples. A student could read the lesson as saying the Church of England conducts same-sex marriages.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Homosexuality and the Church of England.

findings.claim: "Use the technical terms “unitive” and “procreative” ... they appear in the mark schemes for Catholic paper questions." Also "For the 12-mark Discuss".
findings.truth: A claim about the contents of board mark schemes cannot be sourced and breaches the copyright-distancing rule. The 12-mark command word is Evaluate.
findings.evidence: spec command-word table (lines 4280-4340); house rule on mark-scheme wording.

findings.claim: Question [1] typed "3 marks — Describe"; question [4] uses "Discuss this statement."
findings.truth: Describe carries 4 marks in the spec and is not a Paper 3 form; the 12-mark command word is Evaluate.

findings.claim: The Family Group Movement is "founded in France in 1947" (stated in the tooltip, the prose, a flashcard and the glossary).
findings.truth: The founding claim could not be verified on any permitted source. The movement usually named in Catholic GCSE resources is the Passionist Family Group Movement, which began in Australia in the 1970s; France 1947 looks like a confusion with Teams of Our Lady (Equipes Notre-Dame). The spec asks only what the movement does, so no exam mark turns on the date. Options: delete the founding claim from all four fields, or leave it and let Tom check a Catholic Christianity textbook.
findings.evidence: No article found on Wikipedia for Passionist Family Group Movement or Family Group Movement; the Passionists article does not mention it.
findings.ruling: Leave: unverifiable claim (sources 403 / no article); not mark-affecting.

findings.claim: The Pope Francis source is written "Not Just Good But Beautiful".
findings.truth: The spec writes the title with a comma: "Not Just Good, But Beautiful". The date (Humanum Conference, November 2014) is right.

findings.claim: The description runs to 114 characters. Lesson 2 is 103 and lesson 3 is 105.
findings.truth: The validator limit for a lesson description is under 100 characters, so lessons 2, 3 and 4 are over. Not a factual error, but it will fail a strict validator run. Left unedited because it is out of scope for a fact check.

findings.claim: "Catechism 1938 states that “every form of social or cultural discrimination in fundamental personal rights on the grounds of sex, race, color, social conditions, language, or religion must be curbed and eradicated as incompatible with God's design.”" (repeated in the conclusion, the exam tip, a 5-mark scheme, a knowledge check and a flashcard).
findings.truth: That sentence is CCC 1935, not CCC 1938. CCC 1938 reads: "There exist also sinful inequalities that affect millions of men and women. These are in open contradiction of the Gospel ...". The spec names CCC 1938 for gender prejudice, so the edits keep 1938 with its real content and attribute the quotation to 1935.

findings.claim: Question [1] typed "3 marks — Describe"; question [4] uses "Discuss this statement."
findings.truth: Describe carries 4 marks in the spec and is not a Paper 3 form; the 12-mark command word is Evaluate.

summary: Every lesson carries the same two exam-form faults: a 3-mark Describe question (the spec sets Describe at 4 marks and Paper 3 does not use it) and a 12-mark question written with the command word Discuss instead of Evaluate. Three doctrinal misquotations were confirmed against vatican.va (CCC 2226 has no phrase 'first educators'; the discrimination sentence is CCC 1935 not 1938; CCC 67 is misquoted), the Catechism tooltip in L2 defines the Magisterium, the Lourdes cure count is out of date at 70 (now 72), and an argument is misattributed to Cardinal Newman.
